key: Lo! Allah changeth not the condition of a folk until they (first) change that which is in their hearts; and if Allah willeth misfortune for a folk there is none that can repel it, nor have they a defender beside Him.
s: Amid verses on God’s knowledge of the hidden and the open, the surah speaks of a people’s lot; al-Tabari, on 13:11, takes it as the well-being and favour God does not strip away in punishment until they wrong and transgress against one another.

evidence.words: يقول تعالى ذكره: ﴿إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم﴾ ، من عافية ونعمة، فيزيل ذلك عنهم ويهلكهم= ﴿حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم﴾ من ذلك بظلم بعضهم بعضًا، واعتداء بعضهم على بعض، فَتَحلَّ بهم حينئذ عقوبته وتغييره
evidence.gloss: He, exalted be His mention, says: God does not change what is with a people, of well-being and favour, removing it from them and destroying them, until they change what is in themselves of that by wronging one another and one transgressing against another; then His punishment and His changing come down on them.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Ar-Ra’d 13:11, at 1717), the two sentences that follow the angels guarding. Plain sense faithful: 13:8 to 13:10 set out God’s knowledge of what is hidden and open, and 13:11 turns to what befalls a folk; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 13:11 al-Tabari glosses what God does not change as well-being and favour, removed with destruction only when a people change what is in them by wronging and transgressing against one another, and then His punishment falls. The sentence carries his gloss without drift; nothing is taken from Pickthall’s parenthesis. Evidence cut by script from the packet. Entry-check ok.
